Finding: Daily Official List snapshots contain first, high, low, last and cumulative volume/value trade-based fields.
Implication: Official product can supply coherent EOD trade fields needed for an OHLC authority row.

Finding: Opening price is the first on-market sale price of the series for the day.
Implication: First is the exchange trade-based analogue of raw Open.

Finding: High is the highest on-market traded price of the series for the day.
Implication: A same-basis authoritative High must bound the last on-market traded price.

Finding: Low is the lowest on-market traded price of the series for the day.
Implication: A same-basis authoritative Low must bound the last on-market traded price.

Finding: Last/Previous Last is the last on-market price at which a sale occurred; last traded date/time identify whether it is current-day.
Implication: Official trade-based Last is not merely a valuation field.

Finding: EODHD documents open/high/low/close as as-traded values with adjusted_close separate.
Implication: If licensed exact-date rows are acquired, they are structurally suitable for strict raw-OHLC comparison.

Finding: EODData commercial feed documents Symbol, Date, Open, High, Low, Close, Volume.
Implication: It is technically capable of supplying the required core fields under an appropriate licence.
